title: 2011 AMC 12B Problem 14
statement: A segment through the focus \(F\) of a parabola with vertex \(V\) is perpendicular to \(\overline{FV}\) and intersects the parabola in points \(A\) and \(B.\) What is \(\cos(\angle AVB)?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(p=FV\) and let the directrix be \(\ell.\) Projecting \(F\) and \(B\) onto \(\ell,\) the focus-directrix property gives \(FB=2p\) (the distance from \(B\) to \(\ell\)), and by the Pythagorean Theorem \[ \begin{aligned} VB&=\sqrt{FV^2+FB^2} \\ &=\sqrt{p^2+4p^2}=\sqrt5\,p. \end{aligned} \]

Then \(\cos(\angle FVB)=\dfrac{FV}{VB}\) \(=\dfrac{p}{\sqrt5\,p}\) \(=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt5}.\) Since \(\angle AVB=2\angle FVB,\) \[ \begin{aligned} \cos(\angle AVB) &=2\cos^2(\angle FVB) \\ &\quad {}-1 \\ &=2\cdot\dfrac15-1 \\ &=-\dfrac35. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let \(p=FV.\) Use the focus-directrix property to find \(FB\) and then \(VB\)
Find \(\cos(\angle FVB),\) then \(\angle AVB=2\angle FVB\) via the double angle formula
